messages.subject: TMB::normalize question with reproducible example.
parts:
Hello,

I was hoping I could get a better understanding of the syntax for using TMB::normalize.  I have data simulated here where two random effects vectors are distributed from GMRF.

The first model does not use TMB::normalize(), and fits correctly. 
The second one (multiple_gmrf_random_effects_unnormalized.cpp) tries to use flags and TMB::normalize(), and does not seem to converge correctly. 
Does anyone have an idea? 


Thanks,
Dan

library(Matrix)
library(TMB)

compile("multiple_gmrf_random_effects.cpp")
compile("multiple_gmrf_random_effects_unnormalized.cpp")
dyn.load(dynlib("multiple_gmrf_random_effects"))
dyn.load(dynlib("multiple_gmrf_random_effects_unnormalized"))

n<-50000
k<-10
X<-cbind(rep(1, n), matrix(runif(n*k),ncol=k))
beta<-rnorm(k+1)
sd_a<-.3
sd_b<-.1


### GMRF #1 (sparse block diagonal covariance for groups )
Ga1<-matrix(.5, 4, 4)  ## covariance within a group
diag(Ga1)<-1
grp<-rep(1:(n/4), each=4)
Qa<-as(chol2inv(chol(.bdiag(rep(list(Ga1),times=n/4)))), "dgTMatrix")

ua<-as.vector(t(chol(chol2inv(chol(Qa))))%*%matrix(rnorm(n, 0, sd_a), ncol=1))


### GMRF #2 (sparse block diagonal covariance for groups )
Gb1<-matrix(.25, 8, 8)  ## covariance within a group
diag(Gb1)<-1
Qb<-as(chol2inv(chol(.bdiag(rep(list(Gb1),times=n/8)))), "dgTMatrix")

ub<-as.vector(t(chol(chol2inv(chol(Qb))))%*%matrix(rnorm(n, 0, sd_b), ncol=1))

sd(ua); sd(ub)

y<-as.vector(X%*%beta + ua + ub + rnorm(n))

dl<-list(y=y,
     X=X,
     Qa=Qa,
     Qb=Qb,
         flaga=1,
         flagb=1)

parameters <- list(
                   log_sdres = 0,
                   log_sd_a = 0,
                   log_sd_b = 0,
                   a            = rep(0.0, n),
                   b            = rep(0.0, n),
                   beta          = rep(0, ncol(X))
                  )

obj <- MakeADFun(dl, parameters, random=c("a", "b"), DLL="multiple_gmrf_random_effects")
opt <- nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)
### works

dl<-list(y=y,
     X=X,
     Qa=Qa,
     Qb=Qb,
         flaga=0,
         flagb=0)

obj2 <- MakeADFun(dl, parameters, random=c("a", "b"), DLL="multiple_gmrf_random_effects_unnormalized")
obj2<-TMB::normalize(obj2,flag=c("flaga", "flagb"))
opt2 <- nlminb(obj2$par, obj2$fn, obj2$gr)
### doesn't work

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: TMB::normalize question with reproducible example.
parts:
From ?normalize:

"In order for this to work, the model must include a flag that disables the data term so that the un-normalized random effect (negative log) density is returned from the model template."

Example:

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/master/tmb_examples/spde_aniso_speedup.cpp

You only need one flag. Why do you have two?
The template should look something like the following (flag==0 disables the data term as required by the documentation):

  nll += GMRF(Qa, false)(a);
  nll += GMRF(Qb, false)(b);
  if(flag == 0) return nll; // Return without data term
  for( int j=0; j<X.rows(); j++){
    nll -= dnorm( y(j) , eta(j), exp(log_sdres), true );
  }
  return nll;

parts:
Thank you!

I got it work correctly following your suggestion.  I had thought that I might need a separate flag for each unnormalized random effect density. 
One observation is that it seems that the version using TMB::normalize() is slower than the unnomralized, at least on this toy example. 
Is there any intuition behind this?  Does it depend on the sparsity of the GMRF?
Here is modified R code and templates, comparing the time to fit.

(Also wondering, what is the best way to pass a boolean data term to a template?)

Thanks,
Dan
